001: So, for Thursday's presentation, do you already have an idea for the structure?
Yes, I was thinking of starting with the market context, then moving on to our results.
That's a good approach. Do you plan to present the key figures right from the start?
More like in the middle, after explaining the strategy. That will give the data more weight.
I see. And for the conclusion, do you plan to propose concrete action items?
Exactly, I want to end on a dynamic note to encourage discussion.
002: Were you able to prepare the slides for tomorrow's meeting?
Not yet, I still need to refine the part on the financial projections.
Do you want me to give you a hand with the formatting?
With pleasure, especially for the graphs. I always find it complicated to make them clear.
We could use simpler diagrams to illustrate the trends.
Good idea, I'll work on that tonight and send you a revised version.
003: How do you plan to capture the audience's attention from the very start of your presentation?
I'm thinking of opening with a provocative question about our consumption habits.
Interesting. And if some people don't respond, do you have a plan B?
Yes, I can follow up with a surprising statistic to kick off the topic.
That sounds solid. Do you plan to get the audience involved at some point?
Yes, I'm going to offer a quick interactive poll around the middle of the presentation.
004: Have you rehearsed your speech for next week's presentation?
Not yet, I'd rather finalize the content with the latest data first.
You shouldn't neglect the part about the project's potential risks.
You're right, I'll add a slide dedicated to that topic.
And for the timing, have you calculated how much time you'll spend on each section?
About five minutes per part, which leaves us a little leeway for questions.
005: Have you thought about adapting your language for the executive committee?
Yes, I'm going to avoid technical jargon and focus on concrete results.
That's essential. You could also prepare an executive summary to hand out.
Good idea, that will make it easier for the participants to follow along.
Do you want me to review your notes to check the clarity of the message?
That would be great, I really appreciate your critical eye on this kind of thing.
006: For your presentation, did you choose a fairly classic format or a more innovative one?
I was thinking of mixing the two: a clean visual support with a few interactive elements.
That can work well. Do you have a live demonstration planned?
Yes, but I'm going to prepare a video version as a backup in case the technology fails us.
Caution is the mother of safety. Have you also thought about preparing answers to objections?
Yes, I listed the most likely questions and prepared solid arguments.
007: Have you already defined the objectives of your presentation for the client?
Yes, the main objective is to reassure him about our ability to deliver on time.
And how do you plan to illustrate that reliability?
I'm going to rely on examples of similar projects successfully completed by our team.
That's a good strategy. Do you plan to mention the performance indicators?
Of course, I'm going to present a few key figures to support my argument.
008: Have you thought about how you're going to handle difficult questions during the presentation?
Yes, I'm going to stay calm and rephrase the question to buy myself some thinking time.
That's an effective technique. You could also anticipate sensitive topics.
I thought about that, especially regarding the budget. I prepared careful but honest answers.
Do you want to do a Q&A simulation to get you ready?
Excellent idea, that will help me feel more comfortable on the big day.
009: Do you plan to use visual aids to make your presentation more lively?
Yes, I'm going to include a few infographics and maybe a short video.
Be careful not to overload the slides, you need to keep the message clear.
You're right, I'm going to prioritize simplicity and leave the details for the discussion.
And for the conclusion, have you thought about a specific call to action?
Yes, I'm going to propose a concrete next step to follow up on the presentation.
010: Do you feel ready for your big presentation in front of the investors?
Fairly confident, even though I'm still reviewing a few figures to be flawless.
It's good to fine-tune the details. Have you thought about rehearsing with a timer?
Yes, I'm going to do a full run-through tomorrow morning to nail down my timing.
And if your mind goes blank, do you have a strategy to recover?
I'll keep my main notes in front of me, and I can always rely on my slides.
